questions.q: For a scenario needing a rigorous, defensible pre-fault-tolerant hardware-resourcing estimate for a funding decision, which tool does the lesson recommend, and why?
options: Qiskit, because its transpiler is more accurate

Q#/Azure Quantum Resource Estimator, because it is the standardized, integrated, free service purpose-built for exactly this fault-tolerant-planning question, with no equivalent single integrated tool in the Qiskit ecosystem
Neither tool can answer this question
Qiskit, because it is the more widely used tool
questions.explain: This is the clearest case in the comparison: the Resource Estimator is specifically built for exactly this kind of pre-fault-tolerant hardware-resourcing question, a standardized capability the lesson notes has no direct Qiskit-ecosystem equivalent.

questions.q: For building a large, modular, team-maintained quantum codebase where the compiler should catch bugs before code review, which tool does the lesson recommend, and what specific mechanism justifies it?
options: Qiskit, because of its circuit drawing capabilities

Q#, because the operation/function split and compiler-checked functors mean a function cannot smuggle in quantum side effects and an invalid is Adj claim is rejected at compile time, not discovered at runtime
Neither tool supports large codebases
Qiskit, because Python has more libraries available
questions.explain: The specific mechanism cited is the compiler-enforced operation/function separation and functor validity checking from Chapter 2 -- these catch a real class of bugs at compile time rather than relying on code-review discipline alone.

questions.q: For quickly visualizing, transpiling, or programmatically restructuring circuit internals as part of the work itself, which tool fits better, and why?
options: Q#, because operations are easier to inspect at runtime than Qiskit circuits

Qiskit, because its circuit-as-data model and near-term transpilation tooling make runtime circuit introspection and transformation natural, which Q#'s compiled-operation model does not provide an equivalent for
Neither tool supports circuit visualization
Q#, because of its resource estimator
questions.explain: This scenario plays directly to Qiskit's strength established in Lesson 23 (circuit-as-data) and Lesson 24 (transpilation tooling) -- a genuine advantage for this specific kind of work, not a general superiority claim.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what is the 'actual mistake' in choosing between these two tools?
options: Choosing Qiskit over Q# in any circumstance
Choosing Q# over Qiskit in any circumstance
Picking one tool as 'the' answer for every project, rather than matching tool choice to the specific mechanism each task actually needs
Learning both tools instead of specializing in just one
questions.explain: The lesson's framing is explicit: none of the four scenarios are about one tool being better overall -- defaulting to a single favored tool regardless of fit is presented as the real mistake, not which specific tool someone picks.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say this course exists as the second toolchain in the learning path?
options: Because Qiskit is being deprecated and Q# will replace it entirely

Because a quantum software engineer who only knows one tool can only default to it regardless of fit, while real teams increasingly need people who can match tool choice to task and explain that choice using real mechanisms
Because Q# is strictly required for all quantum programming jobs
Because this course has no connection to the earlier Qiskit course in the path
questions.explain: The course's explicit purpose, stated in the wrap-up, is building genuine toolchain fluency -- the ability to reach for the right tool for a given task and explain that choice in terms of real mechanisms, not tool loyalty.
